One person throughout: Rosa, day 34, baseline morning average 148 mg/dL, now 132, the range 80–130 before meals typed in from her own clinic on 3 March. Every string is unreviewed.

S01.headline: Most of diabetes happens between appointments.
S01.sub: Fifteen minutes with a clinician, and then six thousand minutes on your own. GlucoseWise is for the six thousand.

blocks.title: Your numbers stay yours
blocks.body: Readings, notes and check-ins live on your phone. Nothing reaches your clinic unless you send it.

blocks.title: A number can mean call someone
blocks.body: When a reading sits outside the range your clinician gave you, we say so and point you at a person — not at another screen.

blocks.title: It will never tell you what to take
blocks.body: No doses, no amounts, no timing, no calculator. Not once, not as a suggestion. That belongs to you and whoever prescribes for you.

S01.footer: Education and self-management support. Not a diagnosis or treatment.

S02.title: What it does
S02.headline: Four moments this is built for.
S02.sub: Not four features. Four points in an ordinary week where diabetes gets heavy.

blocks.title: When you've stopped looking at the meter
blocks.body: A week of just logging, nothing asked of you. Without a starting picture, neither of us can tell later whether anything changed.

blocks.title: When the walk keeps not happening
blocks.body: One aim, set by you, small enough to survive a bad week. Missing it is data, not a failure.

blocks.title: When the number on the meter scares you
blocks.body: The screen you land on says who to call. It does not interpret the number, and it does not ask you to log it and carry on.

blocks.title: When a day just goes badly
blocks.body: It goes into your history. It never zeroes a count you've built, and nobody is told.

blocks.title: What it isn't
blocks.body: It doesn't read your meter, name a medicine, work out an amount, adjust anything, or tell you what a reading means. If a screen ever looks like it's doing one of those, it's a bug worth reporting.

S02.footer: Education and self-management support. Not a diagnosis or treatment.

S03.title: Consent & privacy
S03.headline: What we hold, and what we don't.

blocks.title: Held on your phone
blocks.body: Your readings, the range you typed in, your check-ins, your notes, your walking aim. These stay local.

blocks.title: Shared with your clinic
blocks.body: Nothing, until you choose. When you do, it's the readings and the dates — never your mood ratings, never what you wrote.

blocks.title: You can leave
blocks.body: Export or delete everything at any point. Deletion is completed, not hidden — your phone, our servers, and anything waiting to sync.

items.title: Let my clinic's nurse see my readings
items.body: Off by default. You'd still approve each send.

blocks.title: One thing you are not consenting to
blocks.body: This is not a route to urgent care. It doesn't watch your readings overnight and it can't call anyone for you. If something is wrong now, use the phone.

S03.footer: You can change either choice later in Settings.

S04.title: Baseline week
S04.headline: Just log, and carry on.
S04.sub: Nothing changes this week. No aim, no nudge. We're only trying to find out where you're starting from.

blocks.title: All three before breakfast
blocks.body: That's the one your clinic asked you for, and it's the one that compares cleanly week to week.

blocks.title: These are numbers you typed in
blocks.body: GlucoseWise doesn't read your meter and doesn't check what you enter. A typo stays a typo until you fix it.

blocks.title: You don't have to wait out the week
blocks.body: Set your aim now if you'd rather. We'll mark the baseline as partial and say so on every chart that uses it.

blocks.title: If a reading worries you this week
blocks.body: Don't wait for the baseline to finish. Call your clinic.

S05.title: Your weekly aim
S05.headline: What could you actually do next week?
S05.sub: Pick something that survives a bad Tuesday. You can move it later, in either direction, with no penalty.

blocks.title: Minutes of walking, on the mornings you walk
blocks.foot: Short and repeatable beats long and occasional, for most people, most of the time.

blocks.title: Mornings a week
blocks.foot: Five leaves you two days of slack before the week is spoiled.

blocks.title: When you'll log a reading
blocks.body: A reminder at the time you pick. On your lock screen it says GlucoseWise and nothing else.

blocks.title: We are not setting a glucose target
blocks.body: There's no slider here for your numbers, and there never will be. The range on your reading screen is the one your clinic gave you and you typed in. Only you can change it, and changing it here changes nothing about your care.

S05.footer: Loosening an aim takes effect straight away. Nothing here waits or argues with you.

S06.title: Review your plan
S06.headline: Your plan is ready.
S06.sub: Have a last look. Any line here can be edited now or later.

blocks.title: Light — one reading, five walks
blocks.body: We'll suggest more only if your own numbers say it would help, and you can say no.

S08.title: Daily check-in
S08.headline: How did today go?
S08.sub: No right answers, and nothing here is a test. It only shapes what we offer you next.

blocks.title: How did your daily care go?
blocks.body: A week where you manage some of it is a normal week, not a bad one.

blocks.title: Medicines as usual today?
blocks.body: Yes or no is all we record. We never ask which ones or how much, and we never tell you what to take or when to change anything.

blocks.title: How heavy did today feel?
blocks.foot: This is how the day felt to you. It is not a measurement of anything.

blocks.title: Some things don't belong in a check-in
blocks.body: Shaky, sweaty, confused, or a reading that frightened you — that's a phone call, and it's worth making now rather than after you've finished this.
Everything on this screen is you describing your own day. GlucoseWise records it as a self-report and never as a clinical finding.

S08.footer: Private · Works offline · You can edit today's answers later

S09.headline: What did the meter say?
S09.sub: The number and the time. Nothing else is needed, and nothing else is asked.

blocks.eyebrow: The range is yours, not ours
blocks.title: 80 – 130 before meals
blocks.body: You typed this in on 3 March from your clinic visit. GlucoseWise didn't choose it, can't change it, and has no view about whether it's right for you. If your clinic gives you a different one, edit it here.

blocks.title: When a number is a phone call
blocks.body: If a reading falls outside the range you entered, we'll say so and stop there. We will not tell you what it means, and we will not tell you to do anything about it. Ring your clinic the same day — that's the whole instruction.

blocks.title: If you feel shaky, sweaty or confused
blocks.body: Treat a low the way your clinician or diabetes educator told you to, and tell whoever is with you. If nobody has ever given you a plan for a low, that is worth a call today and not at your next appointment. If you can't keep anything down, can't help yourself, or someone can't wake you — that's 911.
This screen shows your number and how it's been moving. It does not interpret it. Typed in by you, unchecked by us.

S09.footer: Saves offline · You can edit or delete any reading here

blocks.title: Why the dates are on the front
blocks.body: Anything not checked in eighteen months comes down rather than sitting here looking current.

blocks.title: What this library will never contain
blocks.body: No doses. No amounts. No timing. No carbohydrate ratio, no correction factor, no sliding scale, no rule that starts with your reading and ends with your medicine. Not in an article, not in an example, not as a thing other people do. If you want that conversation it has to be with the person who prescribes for you.

blocks.title: And nothing here knows you
blocks.body: These pieces explain. They don't prescribe, they haven't seen your history, and they can't tell you whether any of it applies to you.

S10.footer: Reviewed before it goes up, and dated so you can see how old it is.

S12.title: Support
S12.headline: A route to a person.
S12.sub: Nothing is sent until you preview it and confirm.

blocks.title: If this is an emergency
blocks.body: Can't keep fluids down, breathing hard, chest pain, too confused to help yourself, or someone can't wake you — call 911 now. Don't finish anything on this screen first.

blocks.title: A reading outside your range
blocks.body: Ring your clinic the same day and tell them the number and the time. GlucoseWise has no opinion about what it means and will not offer one.

blocks.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
blocks.body: Call or text 988 · English and Spanish · 24 hours. Living with this is heavy, and that line is for that too.

blocks.title: American Diabetes Association
blocks.body: 1-800-DIABETES · information and local programs, not urgent care.

blocks.title: Before anything is sent
blocks.body: Every share shows you the exact contents first — readings and dates, never your check-ins or your notes. You can stop at that point, and nothing goes on its own.

S12.footer: Crisis numbers route to United States services.

S13.title: Settings & privacy

blocks.title: Notifications
blocks.body: Detail is off. A reminder on your lock screen says GlucoseWise and nothing else — not which program, not a reading, not why. Anyone who picks up your phone learns that an app reminded you. That's all, and that's the default.

items: Nothing shared · you approve each send

blocks.title: Export everything
blocks.body: A readable file and a structured one: every reading, every check-in, every note, including the ones you've hidden from view. It stays on your phone unless you send it.

blocks.title: Delete everything
blocks.body: Completed, not hidden — your phone, our servers, and anything queued to sync. It can't be undone, and it ends your active programs.
Education and self-management support. It does not diagnose, treat or prescribe, gives no dosing advice of any kind, and is not a substitute for advice from a qualified health professional.

S13.footer: Changing your range here changes nothing about your care. Tell your clinic, not us.
